title: GOES-16 Instrument Anomaly — September 2017 SEP Event
description: On 2017-09-08T16:00:00Z, the GOES-16 EXIS (Extreme Ultraviolet and X-Ray Irradiance Sensor) suite entered a safe mode condition contemporaneous with the largest solar energetic particle (SEP) event of Solar Cycle 24. GOES-16 was in its post-launch on-orbit checkout phase at 89.5°W when the X8.2 flare (2017-09-10) and associated SEP event produced among the highest fluences recorded in Cycle 24. The instrument safe mode occurred during a period of elevated proton flux measured by the co-located SEISS instrument. Whether the safe mode was caused by the SEP environment, by an unrelated software or hardware condition, or by a combination of factors is not established by the available data. All evidence values are derived from publicly archived GOES-16 SEISS Level-2 data (NOAA CLASS). This case is used to validate the multi-case architecture with a second real spacecraft anomaly.
causal_attribution: Causal attribution is not established by the available evidence. The timing of the instrument safe mode relative to the SEP event onset establishes temporal proximity but not causation.

anchor_event.label: goes16_exis_safe_mode
anchor_event.description: GOES-16 EXIS instrument suite entered safe mode. Instrument data transmission suspended. Spacecraft bus and all other instruments remained nominal. Safe mode was cleared by ground command on 2017-09-09.

recovery_event.label: goes16_exis_recovery
recovery_event.description: GOES-16 EXIS resumed nominal science operations following ground command recovery sequence.

data_sources.description: GOES-16 SEISS SGPS (Solar and Galactic Proton Sensor) — 1-minute averaged proton flux channels P1 (1–5 MeV) and P5 (40–80 MeV)
GOES-16 SEISS MPSH (Medium Energy Proton and Heavy Ion Sensor) — 1-minute averaged differential proton flux

scientific_limitations: The GOES-16 SEISS measurements are from the same spacecraft that experienced the anomaly; they are in-situ measurements, not a proxy from a nearby spacecraft. However, the SEISS sensor suite is a separate instrument from EXIS and is not known to have been affected.
GOES-16 was in post-launch on-orbit checkout during this event; sensor calibration and absolute accuracy may differ from operational specifications.

The root cause of the EXIS safe mode is not established: both SEP-induced single-event effects and an unrelated onboard software or firmware condition are plausible. No onboard fault log data is present in this dataset.
The SEP event reached its peak fluence on 2017-09-10, approximately 42 hours after the anchor event; the data window captures only the onset phase.
Ground software and RF link conditions during the recovery sequence are not captured in this dataset.
